summary.text: Kristen Gonzalez is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for re-election to New York State Senate District 59, running unopposed. Raised in Queens, she worked as a staffer for the New York City Council, the Obama White House and Senator Chuck Schumer's office and as a tech worker before winning the seat in 2022. She chairs the Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Internet and Technology Committee.

paragraphs.text: Gonzalez was born in Queens, New York, and raised in a working-class family. According to her campaign website, she grew up in Elmhurst, Queens, with a single mother from Puerto Rico after her father, who was from Colombia, died.
She graduated from Columbia University; her campaign website says she left college to work in Washington, D.C., and finished her degree after returning to New York.

She worked as a legislative staffer for the New York City Council, the Obama White House and Senator Chuck Schumer's office, and, according to her campaign website, as a tech product manager after returning to New York.
Gonzalez organized with the Western Queens Community Land Trust, served on her local community board, and helped launch a citywide campaign for public internet.

She won the Democratic primary for State Senate District 59 on August 23, 2022, with 57.8% of the vote, defeating Elizabeth Crowley, Michael Corbett and others, then won the November 8, 2022 general election on the Democratic and Working Families lines and took office on January 1, 2023. According to her official Senate biography, she is the youngest woman ever elected to the New York State Senate.
She won re-election in 2024 after defeating Gus Lambropoulos in the June 25, 2024 Democratic primary.

Gonzalez is a member of the Children and Families, Consumer Protection, Energy and Telecommunications, Health and Rules committees and the Legislative Women's Caucus, in addition to chairing Elections and Internet and Technology in the 2025-2026 session.
Her legislative work includes protecting private health data to safeguard abortion rights, regulating government use of artificial intelligence, and protecting elections from deceptive media.
She lives in Long Island City.
